suites.name: Protocol unit tests (Python reference)
suites.description: X3DH/PQXDH, double ratchet, envelopes, padding, attachments, session persistence.

suites.name: Adversarial tests
suites.description: Tampering, replay, reordering, downgrade, key substitution, malformed input.

suites.name: Cryptographic test vectors reproduce byte-exactly
suites.description: Regenerates every committed vector (X3DH, PQXDH, ratchet, padding, attachments) and compares bytes. A diff means derived keys changed.

tests.name: tests/vectors/*.json reproduce
tests.details: OK: test vectors reproduce exactly (40047 bytes)

suites.name: Relay (Node) test suite
suites.description: Real HTTP server per test: auth, device-bound sending (A1), prekeys incl. PQ, long-poll, groups fan-out, attachments, blocks, rate limits, migrations.

tests.name: test::registration and login issue usable tokens
test::login failure is identical for unknown user and wrong password
test::protected routes require a valid token
test::database stores no recoverable password or token
test::a one-time prekey is served to exactly one requester
test::prekey exhaustion is surfaced so the client can warn about downgrade
test::a device cannot publish prekeys for another account
test::messages relay end to end and are deleted on acknowledgement
test::offline queue preserves messages until the recipient connects
test::envelope with an unexpected field is rejected
test::oversized and malformed envelopes are rejected
test::a device cannot fetch another device queue
test::a revoked device cannot authenticate or receive messages
test::prekey fetches are rate limited to slow prekey exhaustion
test::security headers are present on every response
test::health endpoint leaks no user metadata
test::internal errors never leak a stack trace
test::queue preserves strict FIFO order within the same second
test::CORS is off by default: no browser origin is granted access
test::an allowlisted origin gets a preflight and CORS headers; others do not
test::a wildcard CORS origin is refused rather than honoured
test::a forged sender device id is refused
test::fetched messages carry the relay-asserted sender username
test::a long-poll returns as soon as a message is queued
test::a long-poll with nothing queued returns empty after the wait
test::batch fan-out accepts good items and rejects bad ones individually
test::the directory resolves usernames to active devices, exact match only
test::usernames are case-insensitive and validated at registration
test::an existing device's identity cannot be swapped by re-registration
test::PQ one-time prekeys are served once each, then the last-resort key

test::attachments are served only to the uploader and listed recipients
test::attachment uploads are size-limited and require a recipient list
test::blocking drops messages silently and hides the blocker
test::reports accept a fixed reason vocabulary and carry no message content
test::presence honours the target settings and is reciprocal

test::logout-all revokes every session of the account
test::account deletion requires the password and removes the account data
test::a v1 database upgrades in place without losing data
test::X-Forwarded-For is honoured only from a loopback proxy, and only when enabled

suites.name: End to end: reference client through the real relay
suites.description: Starts the relay, runs a PQXDH conversation with the Python reference client, then opens the relay database as an attacker would and searches it for plaintext and keys.
